title: Aditya Birla Sun Life Pension Fund NPS Review: Returns, Portfolio & Fees (2026)
description: The National Pension System (NPS) is a long-term retirement savings scheme regulated by PFRDA, offering tax benefits and flexible investment choices. Aditya B.

faq.q: What is the minimum contribution required for NPS?
faq.a: The minimum contribution to an NPS Tier I account is ₹500 per transaction and ₹1,000 annually. For Tier II, it's ₹1,000 per contribution, with no annual minimum.
Yes, any Indian citizen, including NRIs, can open an NPS account. They can contribute using NRE/NRO accounts, and the returns are repatriable subject to FEMA guidelines.

At maturity, up to 60% of the corpus can be withdrawn as a lump sum, which is entirely tax-exempt. The remaining 40% must be used to purchase an annuity, and the pension income from this annuity is taxable as per your income tax slab.

faq.q: Can I change my Pension Fund Manager (PFM)?
faq.a: Yes, NPS subscribers have the flexibility to change their Pension Fund Manager (PFM) once a year. This allows you to switch to a PFM whose performance or investment strategy you find more suitable.

faq.q: What happens if I want to withdraw from NPS before age 60?
faq.a: Partial withdrawals are allowed for specific purposes like higher education, marriage, or critical illness, after 3 years of account opening, up to 25% of your contributions. Early exit before 60 typically requires using 80% of the corpus for an annuity and withdrawing 20% as a lump sum.

faq.q: Are there any guaranteed returns in NPS?
faq.a: No, NPS is a market-linked product, and returns are not guaranteed. They depend on the performance of the underlying investments (equity, corporate bonds, government securities) managed by your chosen Pension Fund Manager.
